paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God wants hearing AND doing. He reminds Judah that the covenant began when He brought their forefathers out of Egypt, saying, "Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God." (Jeremiah 11:4) God never asked for a nod and a smile. He asked for obedience, and He had been asking since the very beginning.

Now here's the sad part. God says He warned them "again and again," yet each one "followed the stubbornness of his evil heart." (Jeremiah 11:7-8) Then He says they have gone after other gods and broken the covenant, and those gods were as many as their cities (Jeremiah 11:10, 13). I think that's what makes this passage so heavy, because the people were sitting right next to the One who rescued them and still went looking for something else. Those gods can't save anybody, and God says so plainly in Jeremiah 11:12.

So what do we take into the bakery today? God had called His people a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit (Jeremiah 11:16), and He is the One who planted them (Jeremiah 11:17). Nothing is better than belonging to the God who planted you, so don't trade Him for a shiny little substitute on every corner. Listen to His Word, then get up and do it, because He is worth every bit of your obedience.
